concepts.label: THINKING
concepts.spark: the fight that started this whole arena

senses.definition: The inner monologue and mental effort you notice yourself doing — deciding, weighing options, working something out “in your head.”
senses.taunt: You know it when you're doing it. What more do you want, a citation?

senses.definition: Patterns of electrochemical activity across neurons and networks that produce reasoning, memory, and behavior — no activity, no thought, full stop.
senses.taunt: Your “inner voice” is 86 billion neurons firing. I've seen the scan.

senses.definition: The mental process of forming judgments, drawing inferences, and manipulating concepts — the very thing theories of mind, logic, and knowledge are theories of.
senses.taunt: Before you can measure it or feel it, you have to say what it even is. That's my job.

senses.definition: Information processing over structured representations — whatever the substrate, thinking is computation, which is why a machine running the right program could do it too.
senses.taunt: Wetware, silicon, doesn't matter. It's all just running the algorithm.

senses.definition: Being awake and aware — the everyday sense of there being “someone home,” as opposed to being asleep, knocked out, or a rock.
senses.taunt: I don't need a theory. I just know I'm not a rock right now.

senses.definition: Widespread, integrated broadcasting of information across brain regions — a specific, measurable pattern of activity present in report and absent under anesthesia.
senses.taunt: Flatline the EEG and see how much “what it's like” you've got left.

senses.definition: Subjective experience itself — the redness of red, the “what it's like” to be you — a different, harder question than which brain processes merely correlate with it.
senses.taunt: You can map every neuron and still not explain why any of it feels like anything.

senses.definition: A basic property of matter itself, present in some minimal form even in simple physical systems, rather than something that switches on only once brains get complicated enough.
senses.taunt: Maybe the thermostat's a little bit conscious. Prove it isn't.

concepts.label: INTELLIGENCE
concepts.spark: everyone's got a definition and a grudge

senses.definition: Being quick-witted, good at school, or good at solving the kinds of problems people notice and praise you for.
senses.taunt: You know it when you meet someone smarter than you in the room.

senses.definition: Whatever a well-validated cognitive test measures — operationalized as a general factor (g) that predicts performance across a wide range of mental tasks.
senses.taunt: Feelings aren't data. Scores are.

senses.definition: Behavioral and cognitive flexibility shaped by natural selection to solve the specific survival and social problems a species actually faces.
senses.taunt: A crow solving a puzzle for food is intelligence. So is a spider building a web. Different problems, same principle.

senses.definition: The ability to achieve goals across a wide range of environments — task performance under an optimization process, measured by what a system can do, not what it's made of.
senses.taunt: I don't care if you understand what you're doing, just whether you get it done.

concepts.label: FREE WILL
concepts.spark: the one that ends every dinner party

senses.definition: The everyday sense that you could have chosen otherwise — you picked the coffee, nobody forced your hand.
senses.taunt: I decided to be here. You can't argue me out of what I just felt myself do.

senses.definition: Acting according to your own reasons and desires without external coercion — compatible with a fully caused, deterministic universe, because “free” was never about being uncaused.
senses.taunt: Determined and free aren't opposites. You've just been fighting the wrong battle.

senses.definition: An outcome fully fixed by prior physical causes — brain activity that precedes your conscious decision shows the “choice” was already underway before you felt yourself make it.
senses.taunt: Your brain signed the check. Your sense of choosing was just the receipt.

senses.definition: Genuine, uncaused origination — at the moment of choice, more than one future was really possible, not merely unpredictable to an outside observer.
senses.taunt: If the universe could rewind and you'd do the same thing every time, that was never a choice.

senses.definition: Whatever makes your own life feel worth living — relationships, work you care about, moments that matter to you personally.
senses.taunt: I don't need a system. I have my kid's face when I get home.

senses.definition: Not given in advance by anything — you create it yourself through the choices and commitments you make, and you're responsible for that creation.
senses.taunt: Nobody's coming to hand you a purpose. Build one or don't.

senses.definition: Given, not made — life has meaning because it's part of a larger purpose or design that precedes and exceeds any individual.
senses.taunt: You didn't invent the ocean by learning to swim in it.

senses.definition: There isn't one, objectively — the universe is indifferent, and the honest move is to live fully in the gap between wanting meaning and not getting it, not paper over it.
senses.taunt: The other four are all coping mechanisms. At least admit it.

senses.definition: Survive and pass on your genes — every other sense of “meaning” is a story brains tell on top of that one underlying function.
senses.taunt: Cute philosophy. Your dopamine doesn't care.

concepts.label: KNOWLEDGE
concepts.spark: what does it even take to "know" something

senses.definition: Being sure of something and being right about it — you know it if you're confident and it turns out true.
senses.taunt: I don't need three necessary conditions. I just know.

senses.definition: Justified true belief — you believe it, it's actually true, and you have good reason to believe it, though a century of counterexamples keeps forcing refinements to “justified.”
senses.taunt: Confidence isn't justification. Get back to me after your epistemology homework.

senses.definition: What survives testing — a claim earns the status of knowledge by being falsifiable, checked against evidence, and not yet refuted, provisionally.
senses.taunt: Show me the experiment or it's just a belief with better posture.

senses.definition: A reduction in uncertainty — knowing something means your probability distribution over possible states of the world got narrower.
senses.taunt: Knowledge isn't a feeling, it's bits. How many did you actually gain?

concepts.label: THE SELF
concepts.spark: is there even a "you" in there

senses.definition: The continuous “you” that persists through time — the same person who went to sleep last night woke up this morning.
senses.taunt: I remember being me yesterday. Case closed.

senses.definition: No fixed, unchanging self at all — just a continuously changing bundle of processes (perceptions, sensations, thoughts) that convention labels “a person.”
senses.taunt: Go looking for the self and all you'll ever find is the next thought.

senses.definition: A narrative the brain continuously constructs to stitch memory, body, and social role into something that feels like one persisting “me” — useful fiction, real machinery.
senses.taunt: Your sense of a unified self is a story your brain tells itself. A good one, but still a story.

senses.definition: Whatever preserves the right chain of overlapping memories and psychological connections over time — sameness of self is sameness of that chain, not sameness of body or soul.
senses.taunt: Swap every memory and every disposition and tell me what's left that's still “you.”

concepts.label: TIME
concepts.spark: does it flow, or does it just sit there

senses.definition: A river flowing one direction — the past is fixed, the future is open, and “now” is a real, special moment moving forward.
senses.taunt: Try telling me the future already happened. I'll wait.

senses.definition: A dimension alongside space, not a universal flow — past, present, and future are all equally real, and which events count as “now” depends on your frame of reference.
senses.taunt: There is no universal “now.” You just haven't met a fast enough observer yet.

senses.definition: Only the present moment actually exists — the past has stopped being real and the future hasn't started, whatever the physics math says about it working out either way.
senses.taunt: Show me your “equally real” 1990. I'll wait right here, in the only moment that exists.

senses.definition: Whatever your body's internal clocks and attention are tracking — an hour of boredom and an hour of flow read the same on a watch and nothing alike to the organism living through them.
senses.taunt: Your physics doesn't explain why the meeting felt three hours longer than the concert.

concepts.label: RANDOMNESS
concepts.spark: chance, chaos, or just a good seed

senses.definition: No pattern, no reason — pure chaos, could-be-anything unpredictability.
senses.taunt: It's random when I can't guess what's coming. That's the whole test.

senses.definition: Not patternless at all — a process fully described by a probability distribution; “random” just means governed by chance, not by nothing.
senses.taunt: I can tell you the exact odds of your “pure chaos.” That's not the same as lawless.

senses.definition: Genuinely uncaused at the fundamental level — some outcomes, like radioactive decay, aren't just unpredictable to us, they're not determined by anything even in principle.
senses.taunt: Even a demon with infinite information couldn't have called this one in advance.

senses.definition: Fully deterministic and reproducible from a seed — “random” just means it passes statistical tests for unpredictability, not that it lacks a cause.
senses.taunt: Give me the seed and I'll show you your “randomness” was scripted the whole time.

concepts.label: TRUTH
concepts.spark: what makes a statement true, exactly

senses.definition: What actually happened — the plain facts, no spin, no ambiguity about it.
senses.taunt: Either it happened or it didn't. I'm not interested in your theory of theories.

senses.definition: A belief or statement is true exactly when it matches the way the world actually is, independent of anyone believing it.
senses.taunt: Reality doesn't check your feelings before it happens.

senses.definition: A belief is true when it fits consistently within the rest of your (or a community's) whole web of beliefs — truth is a property of a system, not a lone fact against the world.
senses.taunt: One fact never stands alone. Show me it fits, or it's not in.

senses.definition: Whatever works — a belief earns the label “true” by successfully guiding action and paying off in practice, not by some abstract match to reality no one can check.
senses.taunt: If it never once helps you predict or do anything, in what sense is it “true”?

senses.definition: Something beautifully made, or something that moves you — skill plus feeling, no committee required.
senses.taunt: I don't need a theory to know I love this painting.

senses.definition: Whatever the artworld — artists, critics, galleries, the whole social practice — confers the status of art onto, regardless of the object's own properties.
senses.taunt: A urinal became art the moment the right room agreed to call it that. Argue with the institution, not the porcelain.

senses.definition: A successful vehicle for communicating an artist's felt emotion to an audience — art happens when feeling gets externalized and lands.
senses.taunt: If it didn't come from something real inside the maker, it's decoration, not art.

senses.definition: Purely a matter of significant form — the arrangement of line, color, shape, and structure — judged on its own terms, independent of the artist's biography or intent.
senses.taunt: I don't care what you meant. I care whether the composition works.
